The page puts the founding at 403 (partition recognised) and Yangzhai as the capital before 375, which the shape misses; Shangdang and Yiyang are added because the Changping and Zhaoxiang pages call them Han's. Cliopatria's Han shape lies north of 34.6 N and holds neither Yangzhai nor Xinzheng, the two capitals the Han page names, and its first shapes contain Anyi, which the Wei page gives as Wei's first capital. Years: the shape holds from 403 to 376; from 375 Zheng is added (next keyframe). Revised 2026-10-19: Anyi, Hedong and Xihe, which the wei dossier holds (Wei page: Anyi first capital; Zhaoxiang page: Hedong), and the Luoyang domain, which eastern-zhou holds, are cut out of every Han keyframe; Cliopatria draws them inside its Han 404 shape, which I read as its mislabelling (its 'Han' 404 contains Anyi and Luoyang, its 'Zhao' 404 Linfen and Changzhi, its 'Wei' 404 the Hebei plain).

ledger.note: 403: the Zhou king recognises Han with Wei and Zhao as marquisates. Infobox 'Partition of Jin: 403 BC'; the Spring and Autumn page: 'the Warring States period began when the three remaining families partitioned Jin' (403) after the Zhi clan fell at Jinyang in 453; the Han page: King Weilie 'elevated their rulers to marquess'. Capital Yangzhai.

ledger.note: 376: Han and Zhao divide the last Jin land. The Spring and Autumn table: 'Jin ... 376 BCE: to Han and Zhao'; the Warring States page: 'In 376 BC, the states of Han, Wei and Zhao deposed Duke Jing of Jin and divided the last remaining Jin territory'. Han's share is not on the page; the disc is Jin's last seat at Yicheng County, Shanxi, the table's location. Dates differ between the pages: the Jin dossier ends Jin in 369 ('modern historians ... generally consider 369 BC the final year', Jin page; dissolve to han at Houma), and the Partition of Jin page has 'In 349 BCE, the Han and Zhao states divided the remaining Jin territory between themselves'. 376 is kept (Spring and Autumn table; Warring States page, re-read 2026-10-19: 'In 376 BC, the states of Han, Wei and Zhao deposed Duke Jing of Jin'); the zhao and wei dossiers carry the matching 376 gain.

'In 230 BC, the Qin army led by Neishi Teng moved south, crossed the Yellow River, and conquered the Han capital Zheng'; Han was 'the first of the seven warring states to be conquered by Qin' (Han page). King An was executed the next year after a loyalist rebellion (Qin page); the Han page dates a rebellion at Xinzheng to 226.

notes:
Han (Hann, 韓; Q1968654). Wikidata Q1968654 is also on Cliopatria's Beylik of Saruhan row (Anatolia, 1314-1414): a different state, no relation; the id is a Cliopatria/Wikidata mix-up, kept as given. Slug collision: this is Cliopatria's 'Han' (-404..-203). Its last shapes (206..-204 and 203) are NOT the Warring States Han: they are Liu Bang's Kingdom of Han (Hàn 漢: 'Sichuan, Chongqing, southern Shaanxi' on the Eighteen Kingdoms page), and are reviewed in the new dossier kingdom-of-han. The Hán row (206-204, Han Cheng, 'southwestern Henan') is han-2 (ea-02) and continues this state; the dossier ends at 207, Cliopatria's handoff. Wikipedia title: Cliopatria's 'Han (state)' is a disambiguation page; the article is 'Han (Warring States)'. Cliopatria's Han shape was placed north of 34.6 N and misses Yangzhai and Xinzheng; the dossier adds discs at Yangzhai (before 375), Yiyang (until 307) and Shangdang (until 262; Cliopatria draws Changzhi in Zhao from 404, which the Zhao dossier subtracts) and the annexed Zheng from 375. The Shangdang disc before 265 is a reading: the pages only call it Han's from 265. Pages opened: Han (Warring States), Qin's wars of unification, King Zhaoxiang of Qin, Battle of Changping, Spring and Autumn period, Warring States period (thin), Eighteen Kingdoms. Not on any page: Yingchuan Commandery (230); the exact year of the Zheng war; Han's wars with Chu, Zhao, Wei, Qi (undated on the Han page); the restoration of 208. Gazetteer names wanted: Yangzhai (Yuzhou, Henan), Xinzheng (Henan), Yiyang (Henan), Qinyang (Jiyuan), Shangdang (Changzhi), Yicheng County (Shanxi), Anyi (Xia County, Shanxi); coordinates used meanwhile.

Revision 2026-10-19 (after review ea-01-d). (1) Anyi: every Han keyframe now cuts the wei dossier's Anyi/Hedong disc (100 km) and Xihe disc (80 km), not only a 45 km Anyi disc, because Cliopatria's Han shapes sit on Wei's Hedong and Henei land as well; K2 and K3 had no Anyi cut. (2) Luoyang: every keyframe cuts the eastern-zhou dossier's own shape (a 35 km disc at Luoyang, its K1-K4); I did not subtract Cliopatria's Later Zhou shapes as the reviewer proposed, because those lie north of the river at Qinyang (34.9-35.5 N) and are Han's Qinyang land before 265, while the eastern-zhou dossier replaced them with the Luoyang disc. After 256 the Zhou domain is Qin's, so the cut stays. (3) New keyframe han_-262 (262-257) without Yiyang and Shangdang; han_-337 now ends in 308 so the keyframes no longer overlap. (4) Daliang: the Daliang disc (60 km at Kaifeng) is Wei's and is cut from Zheng's annexed land. (5) Rulers: Han Cheng 208-207 added from the Eighteen Kingdoms table; the page gives no accession year or capital (confidence 1). (6) Jin's last land: 376 kept, with the 369 and 349 alternatives in L1. (7) L4/L5: the Eastern Zhou page, opened again, shows no transfer; the events stay as Cliopatria's confidence-1 cells and say so. Disagreement with the reviewer: the reviewer's 'minus {cliopatria: Later Zhou}' would also cut Han's Qinyang cells before 265. Han (Warring States) page, re-read: 'Capital: Yangzhai (before 375 BC) Xinzheng (after 375 BC)'; it does not mention Pingyang, Henei or a 208 restoration; 'located in central China (modern-day Shanxi and Henan)'. Addendum: the Zhang Liang page, opened afterwards, gives the restoration year (208) and Yangzhai as the capital, so the 208 ruler, capital and gain are now page-based (confidence 2); the earlier statement that the pages are silent on 208 is superseded. Thin items L8 (Shang Yang) and L14 (Chu 247) were not opened: no page names a Han-Qin or Han-Chu transfer, and the Han page, re-read, lists none. The Wenyu disc of the wei dossier (Wen County, Wei's Henei until the 275 cession) is cut from every Han keyframe as well.
